summary: Independent verification of market.py Bybit error-handling fix (KeyError 'list'). 12/12 pytest passed: Bybit retCode 10006 -> Bitget fallback for klines (300 numeric candles, ts increasing) and tickers (>50 symbols, XRPUSDT price>0); Bybit 403 non-JSON -> fallback OK; Bybit+Bitget failing (500 non-JSON / code 40001) -> stale cache returned (same object) with 'caché' warning, without cache -> RuntimeError starting 'sin datos de mercado para'; _bybit makes exactly 2 attempts; provider=bitget happy path OK. API regression (local 127.0.0.1:8001): dashboard watchlist 6 pairs with price, /api/klines 200, /api/bot/scan -> new 'SCAN Escaneo 1h completado · 6 pares' log within 10s, no ERROR log with 'list'; /api/backtest SOLUSDT 200. Backend logs contain 0 occurrences of 'list'.

minor.issue: Only RuntimeError is caught around _bybit(...)['list']. If Bybit returns retCode 0 but result has no 'list' key (rare), KeyError('list') would still bubble up and skip the Bitget fallback. Suggest catching (RuntimeError, KeyError, TypeError) or using .get('list').
No fallback to previous self.tickers if Bitget also fails; exception propagates (and a non-JSON Bitget body raises ValueError, not RuntimeError). Klines handles this, tickers does not.
Sleeps after the final failed attempt too (extra 0.8s before fallback); with httpx timeout=12s a hanging Bybit can cost ~25s per symbol before falling back.

action_items: Optional: also catch KeyError/TypeError around Bybit ['list'] access so fallback triggers on any malformed Bybit payload
Optional: in fetch_tickers return last known self.tickers when both providers fail
Optional: skip sleep after last _bybit attempt
critical_code_review_comments: Fix is correct for the reported scenario (retCode != 0 / empty result / non-JSON).
_fallback_warned is global across symbols: only 1 fallback warning per 5 min for all symbols (by design, fine).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Market tests patch MarketData.client.get to fake Bybit/Bitget responses; real Bitget used for fallback. pytest.ini forces -n 2; use -n0 for serial/-s output. Bot was running during test so SCAN log is emitted.
rca of the issue: Original: market.py accessed r.json()['result']['list'] without checking retCode; Bybit rate-limit (10006) returns result {} -> KeyError('list') logged by engine.scan_once as '<SYM>: 'list''. Mitigated by _bybit retCode check + retry + Bitget fallback + stale cache; verified.
